title: How Enemas Work
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explain enemas: what they are, how the large intestine and rectum are involved, the history from ancient Egypt and bamboo tubes through Rignier de Groff, Louis XIV, and John Harvey Kellogg, and the medical uses (constipation, fecal impaction, colonoscopy prep, barium X-ray, targeted medication, heat stroke). They cover sexual and BDSM uses, the risks (perforation, sepsis, dehydration, sodium phosphate, water toxicity, alcohol and coffee enemas), and Josh's personal colonic experience. The episode ends with listener mail about cocaine use in the 1970s, tied to an earlier astral projection episode.

segments.title: Opening banter and personal colonic experiences
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck warn about body horror and an adult section, then Josh recounts his past high colonics and his experience getting one, including the farting afterward. They tease the episode's topic.

segments.title: What an enema is and the digestive tract
segments.summary: An enema injects fluid through the anus into the rectum, sometimes reaching the large intestine. They review the digestive tract from mouth through small intestine, ileocecal valve, cecum, and colon, explaining how water is absorbed before waste reaches the rectum.

segments.title: Ancient history of enemas
segments.summary: Enemas appear in ancient texts, with Egyptians using them and the ibis bird myth. Early methods used bamboo tubes and blowing, with the risk of inhalation. Animal bladders and syringes followed, and Rignier de Groff in the 1600s worked on self-administered enemas.

segments.title: Louis XIV and the enema craze
segments.summary: Enemas became fashionable in 17th and 18th century France, with Louis XIV reportedly receiving over two thousand enemas during his reign. Wealthy Parisians showed off ornate syringes. The practice declined when laxatives and pills became common, until John Harvey Kellogg revived it.

segments.title: Historical tobacco smoke enemas
segments.summary: Chuck mentions that English practitioners used tobacco smoke enemas to revive drowning victims, though these reportedly did not work well.

segments.title: How a medical enema works
segments.summary: Describes the fluid volume, which is typically about a liter or two, the positioning, the urge to defecate from fullness and rectal mucosa spasms, and why soapy water is used. Holding the fluid helps soften impacted stool, and patients often cramp.

segments.title: Valid medical uses of enemas
segments.summary: Medical reasons include chronic constipation not relieved by other treatments, fecal impaction, colonoscopy prep, pre-birth enemas (now largely dropped after a early 1980s meta study), barium sulfate X-rays, targeted steroid or medication delivery for colitis, and cooling for heat stroke.

segments.title: Sexual uses, BDSM, and fad appeal
segments.summary: Pre-anal sex cleaning in the porn industry and gay community, with a doctor quoted in Vice magazine saying it is unnecessary. BDSM uses where holding an enema is part of control or humiliation play. Enemas are a wellness fad similar to juice cleanses, linked to Goop.

segments.title: Risks of enemas
segments.summary: Risks include rectal or colon perforation, sepsis, peritonitis, dehydration from sodium phosphate, electrolyte problems affecting the heart, and water toxicity. Alcohol enemas can cause alcohol poisoning. People with heart conditions or colon problems should avoid them.

segments.title: Chuck's colonic hydrotherapy experience
segments.summary: Chuck describes a colon hydrotherapy session at a medspa, with a continuous enema machine, a mirror, and an attendant. He describes feeling either energized or violated afterward, and discusses coffee enemas.

segments.title: Listener mail on cocaine in Morgantown
segments.summary: A listener from West Virginia writes that cocaine was present in Morgantown in 1979 while he attended West Virginia University, responding to Josh's skepticism about cocaine in Ann Arbor. Josh accepts the point. The email is anonymous at the sender's request.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts sign off and give the listener mail address.
